reading.body:
The data describes Lovo as a voice cloning and synthesis product for commercial voiceover, with likeness consent and synthetic media disclosure requirements, but also includes an MCP entry for a different service, Lovora, described as 18+ AI companions.

The product note lists likeness consent and synthetic media disclosure alongside commercial voiceover. That combination matters for AI voice work: cloned voices can be used commercially only when the person whose voice is cloned has consented, and outputs must be labeled as synthetic. The data does not include any cases, so it offers no evidence about how often these requirements are met or enforced.

The MCP entry is inconsistent with the company profile. Its name, slug, and description refer to Lovora, an 18+ AI companion service with companions, prices, content rules, and docs, while the company name and product are Lovo, a voice tool. The data cannot resolve whether this is a merge error or two unrelated entities.

The data contains no information about compute, buildings, or power, so it does not support any claim about AI scaling constraints.
